brief: Equities creep lower into the close on a triple-witching expiration and S&P rebalance, with roughly $7tn of options expiring; GS models close-auction volumes to rise 2-3x versus regular days. GS notes 11 of the past 15 September expirations were down sessions, with selling tending to follow the next week. Crude's spike higher this morning, reversing two days of softer price action, is pushing bond yields higher, with the 10-year retesting 5%. Under the surface, tech drives the bigger moves: the AI basket (GSTMTAIP) extends yesterday's gain (+60bps), while GS's software-vs-semis pair (-3%) gains traction as software (-1.7%) lags semis (+1.4%). NFLX falls 4.4% on a downgrade, with long-only selling and hedge-fund short covering. On Holding rises 1.2% and Nike falls 1.6% after Mbappe signs with On; GS calls the move expected and ties the muted reaction to a 2027 margin debate. Desk flows: overall activity 5/10 and balanced, long-onlys 4% better-for-sale in comm services/healthcare/tech, hedge funds 13% better-for-sale in macro/tech/consumer discretionary. Liquidity is thin (Top of Book ~$1mm) and ETF share of tape is 29%, 2 points above its 20-day average. GS's panic index posted its largest one-day decline in 10 years.
